title: Say it now
hookLine: tell someone what they mean to you

lines: SAID WHILE THEY'RE IN THE ROOM.
cards: At a funeral, someone stands up and says beautiful things. How kind she was. How he always showed up.

How the whole family leaned on her without ever saying so. Everyone nods, and some people cry, and the one person who would most have loved to hear it is the one person who can't. A eulogy is a gift with no address.
What changes when it's said while the other person is still in the room?

teach.b: First, David's lament. When Jonathan dies in battle, David sings a lament for him, and one tender line comes after the news: "I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant hast thou been unto me."
It's a beautiful line. Jonathan never hears it in the song.

teach.h: RUTH SAYS IT ON THE ROAD.
teach.b: Second, Ruth on the road. Ruth's husband has died, and her mother-in-law Naomi tells her to go home to her own people.
Ruth answers while Naomi can still hear: "whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God."
Said to a living face, on a dusty road, those words change what happens next.
Third, Paul names his friends. Near the end of his letter to the Romans, Paul stops teaching and starts greeting people by name. "Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus."
Name after name, with a few words about each: a long way of saying you mattered to me.
Fourth, one sentence, today. It doesn't need to be a speech.
One plain sentence will do: you made this year easier; I think of you when I hear that song; I'm glad you're in my life.
And a look back at the week: plant for later, Marcus Aurelius, Ignatius, memento mori, after me, nothing unsaid, and now, a eulogy. Each one turned the end of life back toward today.

how: Some families and friends make a habit of telling each other what they mean while they are alive, through letters, toasts at gatherings or a simple message, rather than saving it for a eulogy.

o: a written record of a person's last legal wishes
words of praise for someone, spoken at a funeral
a prayer asking God to forgive the one who died

games.q: who said what someone meant — tap the pairs.
p: very pleasant hast thou been unto me
whither thou goest, I will go

s: David's tender line about Jonathan comes in a lament after Jonathan dies
I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan.
Ruth's words whither thou goest are spoken at Naomi's grave
she says them on the road, to Naomi's face.
the end of Romans is only teaching, with no names
Paul greets Priscilla, Aquila and others by name.

games.q: you're Ruth. Naomi tells you to go back to your own people. what do you say?
o: nothing, and you turn for home.
whither thou goest, I will go.
games.why: Ruth stays, and says so to Naomi's face: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God.

practice: Let someone come to mind who means something to you and may not know it, a friend, a parent, a teacher, a neighbor, a child, and hold their face for a few breaths.
Find one plain sentence that says what they mean to you, not a speech, just true, and say it quietly in your head until it sounds like you. If you pray, you can give thanks for them by name.

wordCard.voice: Eulogy, the gift with no address, usually saved for a funeral instead of being said while someone can still hear it. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: you mattered to me. One plain sentence can carry it. That's the week, and day eight hundred twelve.
